reviews.text:
This restaurant, which I saw in Yenny's review, caught my eye because of the macaroni salad rather than the pork cutlet, so I was curious and saved it. It was the weekend, so I thought about going with my family, but I was haunted by the house ghost, so I left my family at home and visited alone.

I saved this house in I want to go and kept track of it when I visited the nearby Panchiya in Sindang-dong or when passing by, but parking seemed difficult, so I took the bus and left.

I was wondering whether I should go to this restaurant again and visit Jeju Donkatsu in front of Sungshin Women's University to calmly taste it, but in the end, I hadn't been there before and decided late to go to this restaurant that seemed to be more suitable for ordering takeout, so I arrived at this place a little late, around 7:20.

There were no customers, but I ordered sirloin cutlet and sat down. I was trying to order a package of tenderloin cutlets for my family, but I couldn't find the tenderloin cutlets. When I asked if the tenderloin cutlets were gone, the male employee said that all the tenderloin cutlets were gone. So I looked and saw that the tenderloin cutlet was covered with a post-it note right below the sirloin cutlet.

Meanwhile, a female customer came in and ordered chicken cutlet. I had no choice but to order chicken cutlet to be safe as I hadn't tasted the sirloin cutlet yet, so I wasn't sure if it would be good for take-out or if it would be tough, and the male employee said he would allow me to place my take-out order by the time I finished eating the sirloin cutlet I ordered.

A female employee who had left when I entered the store came in and served me side dishes of long yellow pickled radish, long pink pickled radish, kimchi, demiglace sauce, tartar sauce, and udon soup. As I listened to the kitchen manager, the female employee, and the male employee talking, it seemed like the female employee was confused as to how the order was placed because she had been out and came back, so they also served tartar sauce. The tartar sauce was slightly sweet because it contained pickles, but it also had parsley, so it was okay, although not as good as the one at Dotori Restaurant in Sangsu-dong, which I recently visited and really liked.

The order must have been mixed up, so the chicken cutlet of the female customer who came later than me came out first, and a little later the sirloin cutlet that I ordered also came out.

Before the sirloin cutlet came out, I asked the waitress for a little more macaroni salad, which I was looking forward to, and it came in plenty. I missed macaroni salad with lots of mayonnaise. In the meantime, whenever I stopped by a Korean-style pork cutlet restaurant, there were places that occasionally served macaroni salad, but in most cases, the mayonnaise was too light and the taste was either bland or watery, so I was looking forward to the macaroni salad at this restaurant because it seemed like it was not just for decoration, but it was still a supporting role to some extent.When I scooped up the macaroni salad with a fork and tasted it, it was slightly sweet, probably due to the corn mixed in. The taste I wanted was something slightly salty and savory rather than sweet, but since it wasn't made so poorly or with almost no mayonnaise, I was satisfied with this alone.

When I looked at the cross section of the sirloin cutlet, it had the same thickness and appearance that I had seen a lot in Yenny's and Kwon Oh-chan's reviews and on the internet. It wasn't a thick cut like the high-end tonkatsu I saw in someone's review online, so I thought to myself that it would have been nice to have that kind of sirloin cutlet.

I dipped it in the demi-glace sauce in front of me and put it in my mouth, okay? Oh, this is demi-glace sauce, not pork cutlet sauce, but the viscosity was good, with a moderately flowing consistency rather than the thick consistency found in thin pork cutlet restaurants in Korea, and the taste was good, so I finally looked up and nodded when I saw the explanation about demi-glace sauce on the wall.

Although it was not of a high standard like Sindang-dong Panchiya, which was manufactured entirely from scratch, it was good because it had a subtle scent of spices and a taste that showed its own level of care and level of not being too sweet. I understand why Yenny said that it doesn't bite even if you eat it thoroughly.

The sirloin cutlet is moist and as if it had been made from surimi, but it is not tough at all and has no unpleasant smell, and although it is not as good as a tenderloin cutlet, it is cut smoothly. However, it doesn't have the good flavor of sirloin like Hannam-dong Rice Meal, so I don't even feel like eating it with salt. By this time, I thought that the sirloin cutlet was okay, so I quickly asked the female employee if I could exchange the chicken cutlet I ordered for sirloin cutlet. The kitchen manager said that the chicken cutlet had already gone into the fryer, so she knew.

The salad topped with Thousand Island dressing, which tasted good, wasn't too watery and was good for a salad served at home in this price range. The udon soup, which wasn't miso soup, was a bit salty, but still not bad. I asked for another refill because I wanted to try the macaroni salad again sometime.

reviews.text:
I visited Yoake, which is famous for being very delicious.
I don't prefer soft food, but it's not easy to come twice due to the distance, so I ordered both on this visit and went with the shio shoyu first!

Ordered shio ramen, ajitama shoyu ramen, and white rice.

The shio ramen had a thicker flavor layer than I expected, and when I concentrated on smelling it, I could smell a subtle pork aroma, but I couldn't detect any other scents, so I tried the soup, and contrary to what it looked like, it came in with a subtle volume. From the middle, the savory flavor and aroma subtly appear, and it seems to come from the chicken, and the aftertaste comes down cleanly and cleanly, like a clear clam broth.
And the chewing of the onions gives it a sweet taste and acts as a refresher.

It feels like eating noodles for the first time
I don't think it's like wheat flour, but it has a unique scent and the texture is medium, but if I had to pick it, it's closer to the soft side.
The soup absorbed well, but I'm not sure if that's because of the noodles.

The menma had a unique, creamy flavor and a subtle sweetness, and the chashu was really delicious.
The smoky and pork aromas are exquisite, and the texture is soft. My mouth is watering even as I write this review.
(It's a shame there are only two, though...)
Ajitamago is lightly seasoned, has less of the fishy aroma and sweetness typical of eggs, and has a more savory flavor, but the lines are clean. So, hmm... I think it might be worth a try even for those who can't eat soft-boiled food.

Shoyu's base is similar or the same as Shio's, so I'll just write down what else I felt.
The sweetness of the soy sauce felt very restrained, and I felt a slight acidity, perhaps because my tongue was strange due to the age. The salty taste of the soy sauce felt like it spread smoothly in my mouth like broth, rather than a sharp or stinging sensation.
As the temperature goes down, the soy sauce becomes stronger, but it wasn't annoying and the change was actually fun.

The rice was very sticky, but I don't know if it was intentional or because it was undercooked.
When I just chewed the rice, it tasted more savory and slightly umami than sweet.

Overall review
The soup is well balanced, has an excellent sense of unity, and has a comfortable taste.
However, it is not just a simple taste; even if you eat it while analyzing it, each layer feels delicate.
I think this is excellent ramen that was made very well.

If I had to point out a drawback, there was little chashu and menma, so I had to eat only noodles and soup from the middle, but because of that, I felt a little bit hungry.

I enjoyed the delicious ramen😀

reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in ramen
Located a 1-minute walk from Exit 10 of Dongdaemun Station.
Tonkotsu ramen size M is 13,000 won.
​
Full of toppings~
It is said to be ramen made by boiling pork and chicken bones and anchovies.
If you look at the ingredients alone, it has quite a strong fusion feel,
If you actually taste the soup, it tastes close to tori paitan.
Surprisingly, tonkotsu has a strong pork smell.
I did not feel the strong anchovy taste of Niboshi Ramen.
Even though it was a rainy day, I couldn't smell the smell of pork at all inside the store.
The ramen tasted like a thick but relatively mediocre soup.
The noodles were cooked just right so I could eat them without any discomfort.
It went especially well with sous vide char siu.
You can choose the size of ramen.
If you like meat like me, size M with lots of meat toppings is good value for money.
However, the pork char siu was a bit dry, so it was a shame to finish eating it.
I expected a soft texture, but it tasted like rough soybean paste.
Instead, the sous vide sirloin chashu is soft and tasty.
I didn't expect much, but it was surprisingly good.
​
Store & Tips & Review
The store is small, with seating facing the wall, making it a good place to eat alone.
It is most suitable for a visit alone or with two people.
Order at the table and pay at the counter when you leave.
They say they give you a drink when you pay with cash or transfer.
At the time of my visit, I did not see the owner chef.
Two foreign employees were in charge of the kitchen and hall.
We sell ramen, maze soba, tsukemen, yakisoba, etc.
It was okay that the prices were different for each size.
The building is a bit shabby and lacks a neat feel,
It was a common atmosphere in Japan, so it didn't bother me too much.

The alley behind the Daehakcheon Book Wholesale Building is filled with grilled fish shops and chicken restaurants. Nowadays, ‘Jinokhwa Halmae Chicken Hanmari’ is the most crowded, but the leader of this alley is ‘Wonso Chicken’ (Wonhalmae Rumored Chicken Hanmari). It has been over 20 years since I visited Wonsan Chicken. During that time, there was a fire and it was closed for a long time.

The highlights of Wonso Chicken are, of course, white kimchi and minced seasoning sauce. I think everyone imitates one chicken in another restaurant, but they can't overcome the subtle differences. Of course, each person's taste is different. After eating all the chicken, if you add the remaining white kimchi and chopped seasoning when boiling the kalguksu, it tastes better than most kalguksu restaurants.

When the fire broke out, some nearby customers were taken away. Many similar businesses have appeared in the alley, and foreign tourist guides are driving tourists to Jinokhwahalmane, so although there are no movies like before, it is still a place with many regulars. Jinwonjo Chicken Hanmari and Myeongdong Chicken Hanmari are also popular single chicken restaurants in this alley.

I tried all of them, but Wonso Chicken suited my taste the best. I have experience going to Myeongdong Chicken Hanmari with people with mobility impairments because electric wheelchairs can fit there. I have good memories of being welcomed so kindly.

In the end, there was a situation where one 600ml bottle was not enough, so I ordered two or three more bottles of Koryochon...
The owner is friendly and doesn't seem to charge a corkage fee if you tell me in advance about the bottle he's prepared.

Pickled cucumbers, which seem to be a basic side dish, are also the best combination to reduce the greasiness of oily food...
The eggplant fritters are also very tasty and have a good texture...
It might be a bit difficult for people who are weak to coriander to make seasoned dried tofu…
